title: Indian Art Auction: Bid for Heritage
description: Step into the world of Indian art and heritage! You have a budget of Rs 50,000 to bid on 8 stunning pieces of traditional Indian art and craftsmanship -- from Madhubani paintings and Thanjavur art to Pashmina shawls and Bidri ware. Compete against AI collectors to acquire pieces at the best prices. Buy low, build a valuable collection, and learn about India's rich artistic traditions!
learning_objectives: Discover India's diverse traditional art forms and their cultural significance across different regions
Learn the basics of auction bidding strategy -- when to bid aggressively and when to hold back
Understand the concept of true value vs. market price and how to evaluate worth under uncertainty
Develop budget management skills by allocating limited funds across multiple competing items
Appreciate the craftsmanship and heritage behind Indian art forms recognised as GI (Geographical Indication) products

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: You start with a budget of Rs 50,000 -- this is all the money you have to spend across the entire auction
Each of the 8 items goes up for auction one at a time with a starting bid displayed
You can place a bid, raise your bid, or choose to pass on an item entirely
AI collectors (Collector Raj, Museum Director Priya, and Heritage Dealer Suresh) will bid against you based on their own strategies
The highest bidder wins the item. If you win, the amount is deducted from your budget
After all 8 items are auctioned, your collection is valued based on the true value of items you won
Your final score is calculated from the total true value of your collection minus what you spent -- maximise profit!
tips: Do not blow your entire budget on the first few items -- save enough for later pieces that might be undervalued bargains
Watch the AI bidders' patterns: Raj bids aggressively on everything, Priya is selective but strategic, and Suresh targets rare items
The starting bid is often well below true value -- but be careful, bidding wars can push prices above true value, turning a good deal into a loss
Sometimes the smartest move is to let an item go and save your budget for the next opportunity

items.label: Madhubani Painting -- Sita's Garden
items.description: A traditional Mithila painting from Bihar depicting Goddess Sita in a lush garden, created using natural dyes on handmade paper. Madhubani art is characterised by geometric patterns, vibrant colours, and mythological themes. This art form has been practised by women in the Mithila region for centuries and received GI tag recognition.

items.label: Thanjavur Gold Leaf Painting -- Lord Krishna
items.description: A Thanjavur (Tanjore) painting of Lord Krishna playing the flute, crafted with 22-carat gold leaf, semi-precious stones, and rich colours on a wooden base. Originating in the Maratha court of Thanjavur in the 16th century, these paintings are known for their surface richness and compact composition. A prized collector's item.

items.label: Pashmina Shawl -- Kani Weave
items.description: An authentic hand-woven Pashmina shawl from Kashmir featuring intricate Kani weave patterns. Made from the fine undercoat of the Changthangi goat found in Ladakh, genuine Pashmina is one of the finest and most expensive natural fibres in the world. A single shawl can take 6 to 18 months to weave. GI-tagged product of Jammu & Kashmir.

items.label: Bidri Ware Vase -- Silver Inlay
items.description: A hand-crafted Bidri ware vase from Bidar, Karnataka, made from a blackened alloy of zinc and copper with intricate silver inlay work depicting floral motifs. Bidri ware originated in the 14th century during the Bahmani Sultanate and is one of the most recognised metal handicrafts of India. It holds a GI tag from Karnataka.

items.label: Pattachitra Scroll -- Jagannath Trilogy
items.description: A Pattachitra painting on cloth depicting the Jagannath trilogy (Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra) from the Raghurajpur artist village in Odisha. This ancient art form uses natural colours derived from conch shells, lampblack, and local stones. The intricate border designs and mythological narratives are hallmarks of this UNESCO-recognised tradition.

items.label: Dhokra Brass Horse -- Lost-Wax Casting
items.description: A Dhokra brass horse figurine created using the ancient lost-wax (cire perdue) casting technique, one of the earliest known methods of metal casting dating back over 4,000 years to the Mohenjo-daro civilisation. Crafted by tribal artisans of Bastar (Chhattisgarh) and Bankura (West Bengal), each piece is unique as the wax mould is destroyed during casting.

items.label: Miniature Painting -- Mughal Court Scene
items.description: A Rajasthani miniature painting depicting a Mughal court scene, created using fine brushwork on handmade wasli paper with natural pigments including gold dust, lapis lazuli, and vermillion. Indian miniature painting flourished under the Mughal, Rajput, and Pahari schools between the 16th and 19th centuries. This piece features the Kishangarh style famous for its 'Bani Thani' portrait tradition.

items.label: Channapatna Lacquerware Chess Set
items.description: A hand-turned and lacquered wooden chess set from Channapatna, Karnataka -- known as the 'Toy Town of India'. The pieces are crafted from ivory wood (Wrightia tinctoria) and coated with natural lacquer dyes derived from vegetable colours. Channapatna toys have a 200-year-old heritage dating back to Tipu Sultan's reign and hold a GI tag. A functional art piece that combines play with tradition.

ai_bidders.name: Collector Raj
ai_bidders.description: A wealthy art enthusiast who bids aggressively on most items. He has deep pockets and is not afraid to overpay for pieces he likes. He tends to drive prices up quickly.
ai_bidders.bid_tendency: overbids by 10-30% on items he targets

ai_bidders.name: Museum Director Priya
ai_bidders.description: A knowledgeable museum director who bids strategically. She knows the true value of most items and rarely overpays. She targets historically significant pieces -- paintings and sculptures.
ai_bidders.bid_tendency: bids close to true value, drops out if price exceeds 110% of true value

ai_bidders.name: Heritage Dealer Suresh
ai_bidders.description: An experienced dealer who looks for undervalued items. He bids conservatively and targets items where the starting bid is well below true value. He prefers rare crafts like Bidri ware and Dhokra.
ai_bidders.bid_tendency: bids on items with high value-to-starting-bid ratio, drops out at 80% of true value

glossary_terms.definition: A public sale in which goods are sold to the highest bidder. In an English auction (the most common type), the price starts low and bidders raise it until only one remains. Other types include Dutch auctions (price starts high and drops) and sealed-bid auctions.
glossary_terms.example: Christie's and Sotheby's are famous international auction houses. In India, works by artists like M.F. Husain and S.H. Raza have sold for crores at auctions.

glossary_terms.definition: The actual worth of an item based on its craftsmanship, materials, rarity, historical significance, and cultural importance -- as opposed to its market price, which can be higher or lower depending on demand and competition.
glossary_terms.example: A Pashmina shawl's true value reflects months of hand-weaving, rare Changthangi goat fibre, and centuries of Kashmiri tradition. Its market price at auction may be higher (if many bidders want it) or lower (if buyers are uninformed).

glossary_terms.definition: A sign used on products that have a specific geographical origin and possess qualities or a reputation due to that origin. In India, GI tags are registered under the Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999 and protect traditional crafts and products from imitation.
glossary_terms.example: Darjeeling Tea, Banarasi Sarees, Mysore Silk, Tirupathi Laddu, Kolhapuri Chappals, and Bidri Ware all hold GI tags that certify their authenticity and origin.

glossary_terms.definition: The process of distributing a fixed amount of money across different needs or opportunities. Effective budget allocation requires prioritising high-value opportunities while maintaining reserves for unexpected needs.
glossary_terms.example: In this auction, spending Rs 30,000 on the first two items leaves only Rs 20,000 for the remaining six -- poor allocation may mean missing a bargain later.

glossary_terms.definition: A traditional Indian art form originating in the Mithila region of Bihar. Characterised by geometric patterns, vibrant natural dyes, and depictions of nature and mythology. Traditionally painted by women on walls and floors during festivals and ceremonies.
glossary_terms.example: After the devastating 1934 Bihar earthquake, a British colonial officer discovered Madhubani wall paintings, bringing this ancient art form to global attention. Today, Madhubani art adorns everything from sarees to railway station walls.

win_conditions.description: Build the most valuable art collection within your Rs 50,000 budget! Your score is based on the total true value of items you win minus what you paid. Smart bidding and budget management are key -- buy undervalued treasures and avoid overpaying in bidding wars!
